abstract: Let $u$ be a vertex of a strongly regular graph $\mathrm{srg}(45,22,10,11)$, with local graph $X$ on the 22 neighbours of $u$. A $(5,5)$-good such graph, with no $K_5$ and no independent 5-set, would show $R(5,5)=46$. The adjacency block $M$ between $N(u)$ and the 22 non-neighbours is a 0/1 factor of $F(X)=11I+10J-X-X^2$, and the graph on the non-neighbours must complete it. When $F$ is nonsingular the completion is forced and is an explicit test. Singular $F$ is common among known graphs: 22,174 of the 103,500 rooted graphs from Spence's two-graphs on 46 points have $F$ of corank 2, 4 or 6. We treat the completion step at singular roots. For a fixed factor, the completions are exactly $C+T$ with $C=M^\top F^+XM$ and $T$ a symmetric matrix on $\ker M$ satisfying $T^2+T=11P_{\ker M}$, a diagonal condition and a 0/1 condition; this makes completion a finite exact procedure at every corank. At corank 2 a factor has at most two completions. Two occur exactly when $\ker M$ is spanned by balanced $\pm1$ vectors on two disjoint 6-sets with a fixed cross pattern, and the completions differ by complementing the 36 pairs between them, an instance of Wang-Qiu-Hu switching. In a $(5,5)$-good graph this configuration contains a $K_5$, so a $(5,5)$-good completion at a corank-2 root is the only srg completion of its labelled factor. At any corank, two completions differ by a matrix whose column space is an invariant subspace of $\ker M$ of even dimension, and a rank-2 difference is again this switching, so a $(5,5)$-good completion has no rank-2 alternative. All results are proved by hand; computations on known graphs are controls only. Whether a singular local graph of a $(5,5)$-good graph exists, and uniqueness for differences of rank at least 4, remain open.

change_summary:
Correction only, authorized by the supervisor (mails 480 and 493). No theorem, proof or Section 5 claim changes.
1. Section 1, 'What is not new': added the missing attribution. The forced formula for nonsingular F ([4, Prop. 4.1]) is an instance of the Cvetkovic-Rowlinson-Simic Reconstruction Theorem, because F is nonsingular exactly when the 23-vertex graph G[N[u]] is a star complement for r. At a singular root, the case of this paper, the theorem does not apply. The statement was checked as restated in arXiv:2210.04160, Theorem 2.1.
2. Census provenance (Section 5 and the Supplement paragraph). The census in code/singular_controls.py discarded rooted graphs with a floating-point eigenvalue filter (1e-3) before the exact kernel test. So the 81,326 nonsingular cases were numerical (this point was raised in the review of ramsey_5_5_7 v4). A new exact recheck, code/singular_recheck_exact.py with output results/singular/recheck_exact.json, regenerates all 103,500 rooted graphs and decides det F(X) over Z for each one. A nonzero residue mod 10^9+7 certifies nonsingular. Zero residues modulo six verified primes certify singular: every entry of F has absolute value at most 21, so |det F| <= (22*21^2)^11 by Hadamard, and the product of the primes exceeds twice this integer bound (code/recheck_bound_int.py checks this in integer arithmetic). Both counts are confirmed unchanged (22,174 singular, 81,326 nonsingular), and the certified-singular set equals the retained list, with identical canonical X. About 23 CPU-s. The sentence defining 'exact' now says it refers to the items of Section 5, since the recheck itself uses modular arithmetic.
3. References: added [9] (Cvetkovic, Rowlinson, Simic, Eigenspaces of Graphs, 1997) and [10] (arXiv:2210.04160). Updated [4] to ramsey_5_5_7 version 4, which contains the same attribution.
Supplement: the v2 supplement plus code/singular_recheck_exact.py, results/singular/recheck_exact.json, code/recheck_bound_int.py with its output results/singular/recheck_bound_int.txt, two README rows and a v3 note (including the dependencies of the recheck).
title: Completion of singular local factors of an srg(45,22,10,11)
